claims.statement: Shared preload initializes shared memory and the static launcher; loading pg_trickle outside shared_preload_libraries leaves background scheduling and shared memory disabled.

The launcher discovers databases, checks existing schedulers, and dynamically starts per-database schedulers, with standby promotion waiting and installation/respawn backoff rather than a guaranteed fixed discovery period.
Coordinator startup recovers interrupted refresh records and reconciles parallel jobs and worker tokens before normal scheduling.

Parallel dispatch reserves capacity before durable enqueue, persists unit metadata and immutable dispatch tick bounds plus slot generation, and defers spawning until after the enqueue transaction commits.

A refresh worker promotes its generation-tagged reservation, claims QUEUED work, rejects generation mismatch, missing immutable tick bounds and obsolete DAG jobs, and persists outcomes before normal token release.

Interval freshness targets use persisted next_due_at controller state; controller proposals consider pending age, queue delay, compatible mode cost, load, overrides and memory-constrained batch sizing, conservatively making pending work with unknown age due.
Freshness-controller status distinguishes insufficient data and unavailable evidence from meeting or at-risk targets, with separate sample-aware hysteresis for breach and infeasibility transitions.
Legacy duration schedules use last_refresh_at including no-data runs, with optional tier multipliers and stable jitter; cron schedules use cron due matching without tier multipliers.
CALCULATED nodes inherit the minimum effective downstream schedule in the DAG, while runtime due checks depend on upstream pending changes.

Ordinary scheduler checks exclude EXTERNAL, MANUAL and IMMEDIATE tables before initialization checks, and worker execution also guards EXTERNAL members; FULL non-immutable queries may need reevaluation without source changes.

The execution-unit DAG collapses diamond consistency groups and IMMEDIATE closures, preserves inter-unit dependencies, and supports singleton, atomic, repeatable-read, cyclic SCC and fused-chain units.

Diamond fastest policy schedules when any member is due while slowest waits for all; singleton execution uses READ COMMITTED, grouped execution is transactional, and repeatable-read groups explicitly upgrade isolation.

Dispatcher success advances downstream readiness, but its wave-completion succeeded flag is also used after permanent failure or exhausted retries to prevent permanently blocked waves and does not imply successful data refresh.

Shared-memory coordination uses lightweight locks and atomics; bounded DAG invalidation overflow forces a full rebuild, and database scheduler slots keep database-local scheduler, queue and tick state.
Worker-slot bind, promotion and release match generation identities, while dispatch admission combines cluster/PostgreSQL/adaptive limits with per-database quota and burst capacity.
Worker capacity reservations and correctness tick watermarks are separate: dispatch requires a watermark to enqueue and workers reject jobs missing the immutable dispatch bound.

Refresh exclusion uses transaction-owned catalog-row FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED locks; internal subtransaction guards restore PostgreSQL memory context and resource owner on commit, rollback and unfinished drop.
The pg_trickle memory budget bounds owned accumulation components, treats storage limits as guards rather than lossy caps, and permits component overrides only to tighten derived limits.
Delta-template caches are backend-local and flushed lazily when the shared cache generation advances, independently of worker-slot generations and DAG versions.
Load shedding applies to sequential and parallel scheduling without discarding committed buffered changes, and parallel work also honors pause and retry-backoff admission gates.

Retryable job failures update per-root retry state, successes reset it, permanent failures set member ERROR state as a safety net, and dead-worker reconciliation reaps orphaned jobs and stale slots using live-process and queued-job evidence.

The coordinator processes SIGHUP configuration reloads and drain requests even when scheduling is disabled, skips scheduled work when enabled is off, keeps capture active during CDC consumption pause, and cleans up scheduler metadata on SIGTERM or detected extension removal.

worker_pool_status exposes capacity, adaptive and queue diagnostics; parallel_job_status exposes queued/running and recently completed jobs with PIDs and timing, using a default 300-second recent window.
Coordinator shared last-wake diagnostics are refreshed on a periodic sixty-second cadence rather than every scheduler tick.
Monitoring distinguishes schedule staleness from exact source-commit-to-visible freshness percentiles; no-data staleness uses last_refresh_at and never-refreshed stale status remains unknown.
The pg_trickle_alert NOTIFY event contract includes failure, falling-behind, buffer, watermark and freshness events, with some scheduler reminders throttled using successful emission time.

The optional scheduler-hosted OpenMetrics server is disabled at port zero, uses bounded nonblocking request processing and collection deadlines, and warns without stopping refresh scheduling when binding fails; each per-database scheduler attempts its own configured listener.
Prometheus interval-target freshness metrics read bounded controller summaries rather than reconstructing percentile history during scrapes.

Optional tracing propagates W3C session trace context through CDC buffers and emits spans when enabled with an endpoint; asynchronous best-effort export does not fail refresh execution, and endpoint-configured freshness metric export has a separate periodic path.
Focused worker E2E tests cover automatic schedule refresh, history persistence and a bounded disabled-scheduler no-refresh window followed by reenablement.
Concurrent-DAG E2E tests exercise inter-layer DML visibility, concurrent-insert convergence and rollback isolation using staged refreshes, rather than proving every dynamic-dispatch grouping policy.
Focused monitoring tests cover no-data stale reporting, unknown stale status before first refresh, and cache-stat shape and monotonicity.
